The pilot targets 5,000 hectares across 10 municipalities (starting with Pototan), with three private sector operators — Mayani, Straw Innovations, and Cool Mill — providing inputs/finance, machinery-as-a-service, and efficient milling respectively. Governor Defensor raised the possibility of local assembly or light manufacturing of Straw Innovations machinery in Iloilo, with Sir Jerome's team identified as a potential investor link — this is an open action for BCG to facilitate. Ellen Anthony flagged UK drone/mangrove work as a potential adjacent collaboration. Key open questions include confirming the deployment timeline for the initial 6 Straw Innovations units, formalizing Mayani's pilot onboarding, and defining the path to full 140,000-hectare scale-up.

meetings.title: Water service model for farmers
meetings.summary: The meeting covered Agria Foundation's integrated model for transitioning ~1,000 smallholder farmers in Negros from sugar cane to ube and vegetables, anchored by a farm school, cooperative structure, and blended finance (90% grant / 10% equity under Julie's proposal). Key economics were discussed — ube yielding ~₱480,000/hectare revenue vs. sugar cane in the ₱120–170/kg range, with vegetables potentially reaching ₱1M/hectare/year — though final numbers are to be verified and sent to Sherry for facility sizing. The model preserves a base level of sugar cane productivity (targeting 30–40% improvement via intercropping) to protect mill, trucking, and factory jobs that depend on sugar supply. Funding sources identified include ADB's $200M agriculture program, Thai bank (Dan Bank) agri-law budgets, DA devolution funds, and impact financiers attracted to the women-led cooperative structure. Immediate next steps are for Jamie to review yield estimates this weekend, finalize the investable proposal with Sherry, align with DA, and then engage DTI on market access and export.

meetings.title: Discussion with Djoey
meetings.summary: Jamie and Sue debriefed on Djoey's performance, which remains behind on qualitative PSI and slide writing, with limited observation data to support a confident B rating. A pattern of inconsistency was flagged — Djoey appears to describe situations differently to different people (e.g., framing Sue's request for an adult conversation with Eric as being 'forced to apologize,' and complaining about Home Credit's learning curve privately while affirming it positively to Sue). Sue stated that continued reports of this nature would make it impossible for her to support Djoey staying at BCG, citing character as a critical factor. The three-way conversation tomorrow at 3PM will focus on remaining dimensions, concrete action plans, and explicitly surfacing character/professionalism as a theming dimension — with less focus on feelings. Open question: whether and how to directly address the inconsistent narratives with Djoey without revealing the source.

meetings.title: Discussion
meetings.summary: Jamie and Sven (Inverto) aligned on the approach for an upcoming first engagement session with Meralco, a ~$2B annual spend opportunity across generation and distribution. The planned session is broad-audience with only ~20 minutes for procurement; Inverto's standard approach will be used: capabilities overview, 1–2 AI procurement demos, utility case studies, and an offer of a free Inverto Diagnostic with 4–5x ROI framing. **Open question:** whether SEA utility case studies exist (Sven to check with European Inverto colleagues; Jamie to send Chicago-sourced links). Jamie will use a WhatsApp contact at Meralco to informally gather capex/opex split, procurement team size, and recent transformation programs before the session.

meetings.title: Teaming discussion

The team agreed to reinstate morning no-meeting blocks, consolidate client meetings into dedicated day blocks (Tuesdays lighter, government meetings Wed/Thu, Fridays protected), and explore a full heads-down day weekly or biweekly. Jan flagged that weekly outputs and long-term milestones (heads of terms) are not yet converging and that work across different partners is not repurposable — the team will look to Claude and other AI tools to help solve this. Max proposed shifting milestones from output-oriented to outcome-oriented (documentation into a master doc), which Jamie agreed to raise with the central team; a theming refresh with new ACs and Barry (on AI norms) is scheduled for next week.

meetings.title: GG contract and intervention outputs — WE contributions, targets, and log frame alignment with Moxie and Nick
meetings.summary: The team reviewed the GG intervention's WEE contributions, output targets, and outcome indicators for the upcoming log frame submission. Philippines targets a WEE score of 1, with a mix of selection-stage and delivery-stage contributions across workstreams; a short WEE macro narrative on climate and gender should be added as contextual support. On outputs, substantive business engagements (1.3) will be kept at low (50) with the event as the primary route; outputs 2.2 and 2.3 will reflect a narrative of doubling down on mature projects for conversion rather than generating new outputs, with a broader discussion needed with Tetra Tech and FCDO on double-counting high-potential opportunities across phases. Output 3.2 (commercial partners database) has a low bar and the existing shared database likely already qualifies, while Output 3.3 (AIPs) needs Tetra Tech confirmation. Nick will update the log frame table and send Maxine specific questions for Tetra Tech review; the jobs-created indicator under Outcome 2.1 remains unresolved and will be escalated centrally with FCDO.

meetings.title: Iloilo rice value chain — ratoon cropping, MOU signing, and concept note with Straw Innovations and IPG
meetings.summary: The team aligned on plans for the **August 18 Iloilo visit**: BCG will lead a governor project update (skeleton deck due Thursday 13 Aug), followed by an MOU signing with Straw Innovations and IPG (pending Jeron confirmation), a farmer association roundtable led by Straw, and a closed-door session with Jeron covering RPC pricing, profit share, the IPG guarantee pool, and co-op mill sizing. On the **Temasek concept note**, the two-pager targets 1,000 ha (Phase 1) and 10,000 ha (Phase 2), with a total budget of ~480M pesos and a 1M SGD ask (~22% of total); operators must validate Phase 2 machine counts (56 harvesters/40 mills) and co-financing sources before Friday's submission via Jeff (MyAni). A key open question is how to handle the **capex valley-of-death** for unconventional equipment — options are a longer phased timeline or a bold short burst with an explicit risk register entry on asset funding, with Jamie to frame a recommendation. John flagged that **IPG must be pressed to formally commit as an off-taker**, as the entire end-to-end model depends on it. Additional funding windows (Common Fund for Commodities, UN CTCN, impact investors) were noted but have barriers; BCG will pursue warm contacts and share findings with the consortium.

meetings.title: Straw innovations — MOU signing, concept note refinement, and funding strategy with Greg
meetings.summary: The meeting with Greg (Straw Innovations) covered three main areas: MOU signing, the Temasek concept note, and Straw's funding and operational situation. The ceremonial MOU signing is tentatively scheduled for **Tuesday August 18** pending authorization confirmation from Jeron tomorrow, with Brian, Anne, and British Embassy representatives expected to attend alongside a farmer round table. On the concept note, Temasek (Z) is emphasizing sustainability beyond the pilot, co-funding partners, and a credible aggregator (Mayani flagged as natural fit); Jamie needs to lock in target outcomes, budget allocation by activity/operator, and the scaling pathway in tomorrow's meeting. A key constraint is that **Temasek will not fund capex**, meaning Straw's six combine harvesters are the initial input and broader scaling requires separate financing — Greg suggested spreading this over 3–4 years as part of a wider funding package including potential sources such as Atmosphere (~$1M loan), A2D/UNIDO (~$5M, targeting next round), and the Food Planet Prize ($1.5M, currently top 50). Greg also flagged UK team reductions from end of August (Leo moving to part-time/PhD focus, Alexis pausing), with resources being redirected to Philippine operations.

meetings.title: Discussion with James on the NAP
meetings.summary: The meeting with James covered AIP progress across four workstreams: project development, ecosystem mobilisation, governance, and institutionalisation. The TOR signing has slipped from 3 September to a January steerco, but the September 3 meeting remains action-oriented—principals will commit to roles, provide staff, and agree specific asks (e.g. NWRB water rights). CCC's proposal to incorporate AIP into a department circular is seen as a stronger long-term anchor than chasing the September deadline. On investment reporting, two separate tracks must be maintained—UK Export Wins (BEIS/DBT lens) and overall capital mobilisation (Growth Gateway/Republic lens)—with the core counting principle being net-new, incremental investment only. Open questions include where partner matching parameters will be stored (a Salesforce-type system is needed), how to mitigate relationship managers going cold once BCG ramps down, and whether PBSP should be reframed away from co-chair status in favour of CCC/DOF ownership.

meetings.title: Teaming discussion on August 19
meetings.summary: The team held a teaming refresh to align new members (Alex and two new associates) on system norms, working styles, and case cadence for NAP. Key decisions include: daily 10 AM check-ins, CTM on Mon/Wed, teaming on Tue, weekly post-check-in on Wed, Thursday evening blackout biweekly, and a Tue/Wed vs Thu/Fri module meeting split for operator versus government engagements. Jamie's priority focus this phase is BD-heavy workload rather than execution, with Jan owning day-to-day process and fielding client asks before escalating. Open questions include fully onboarding new members to CaseOS and establishing the cadence for brown bag sessions. Team norms around weekend comms blackout, never immediately saying yes to client asks, and proactive capacity flagging were reinforced with new members.

meetings.title: Adaptation investment planning
meetings.summary: The meeting reviewed progress on the 40-billion-peso AIP portfolio across four provinces, covering climate-smart irrigation, on-farm adaptation, watershed solutions, and post-harvest logistics; approximately 30M pesos has been deployed with a target of 60M pesos in coming months, including a newly signed MOU between Raw Innovation, Cool Mill, and the Iloilo provincial government. The Secretary stressed that climate analytics and industry impact framing must be made far more explicit and direct — particularly the link between AIP activities, NAP outcomes, and quantified sector losses (e.g., ~8B pesos/year at risk in Negros sugar by 2050) — before any presentation to the President. The Secretary directed that 'deal orchestration' be replaced with 'partnership orchestration' throughout all materials, and flagged DBM as an additional institution to invite to the Steering Committee. A three-tier governance structure (Steering Committee, Management Team, Working Team) is being finalized, with the Steering Committee meeting set for 3 September at the DBM office, co-chaired by DOF and CCC as IDSF co-chairs alongside PPP Center. Key open questions include how to operationalize the impact assessment and feedback loop into subsequent NAP cycles, and how to finalize FTE commitments from DOF, PPP Center, and DDSB.

meetings.title: Adaptation Investment Platform — steering structure, agency roles, and terms of reference
meetings.summary: The meeting focused on finalizing the governance and terms of reference for the Adaptation Investment Platform (AIP), including steering committee composition, agency roles, and advisory linkages. A key decision was to move toward a **two-co-chair structure** (DOF and CCC Vice-Chair) rather than three, with PPP Center positioned at the working/secretariat level; the TOR currently sits with DOF for review on lead/co-chair language. Open questions remain around CCC's operational capacity to convene technical advisors given its small team, and whether the existing Interagency Task Force on Sustainable Finance instrument is sufficient or requires a separate resolution. A **September 3 organizational meeting** is targeted to align on structure and ideally advance TOR sign-off, with 1–2 preparatory working-level meetings needed beforehand. BCG (Jamie's team) owns coordinating these pre-meetings, updating slides, and ensuring all AIP materials are anchored to the NAP and clearly distinguished from the LGU Annual Investment Plan acronym.

meetings.title: Discussion with DOF

The agreed framing is that the AIP secretariat is coordinated by PPP Center and PBSP, convened by CCC, with DOF retaining policy oversight and capital access/GCF NDA functions — avoiding language that positions CCC as day-to-day lead. For legal mandate, the interim basis will be the existing ITSF mandate/meeting minutes, with a separate Department Order (DO) to be pursued in coming months and ideally announced alongside TOR signing on September 3. Key open questions include whether DOF principals will clear TOR modifications in time for September 3 signing, and whether Sec. Borh will agree to issue the DO; if TOR cannot be signed, September 3 will be reframed as an alignment meeting with a subsequent signing as the comms moment. Jamie must immediately update the TOR, send it to Jan and in parallel to PPP Center/PBSP, consult CCC tomorrow, and send the advance September 3 invite by end of day August 19.

meetings.title: Avoid this energy valuation — levers, assumptions, and retail market opportunity
meetings.summary: The team reviewed the Aboitiz value sizing model, which now covers 7 levers (down from 8, with RE generator forecaster deprioritized) yielding a $76M–$149M USD range. Six levers were adapted from SIM Corp with high confidence; two lower-confidence levers are corporate function (top-down 15–25% efficiency on PHP 9.8B personnel cost) and distribution O&M (benchmarked against Morocco's 5.9% system loss vs. Aboitiz's ~9.4–10%). Key refinements agreed: confirm the regulatory system loss cap (~6.5%) to split cost pass-through vs. Aboitiz absorption, add a capacity factor improvement sub-lever under thermal O&M bridging coal assets to ~92%, and add a per-1% system loss sensitivity callout. The RCOA threshold reduction from 500kW to 100kW significantly expands Aboitiz's B2B retail opportunity (folded into lever 3), with potential to compete for CNI customers currently served by Meralco (~$1.3B revenue exposure). Marco meeting prep should focus on a single waterfall with key assumptions; the interest component on CapEx savings is an open question to raise with him.

meetings.title: Earthquake resilience event
meetings.summary: An earthquake resilience summit featured presentations on business continuity planning, public-private partnerships, and community preparedness. Key themes included the importance of pre-disaster public-private agreements (citing Japan's 1,000+ Tokyo Metropolitan Government partnerships), the all-hazards BCP approach focused on critical functions rather than specific scenarios, and the need for genuine collaboration rather than mere coordination or cooperation. Sir Rafi Alunan (MAP) identified leadership failure—not lack of plans or funding—as the primary gap, and noted MAP is monitoring ~1,400 member businesses on resilience readiness. A cooperative representative highlighted a grassroots disaster cadet model across ~230,000 weekly centers serving 9.2M clients as a potentially powerful community preparedness network. No direct action items for Jamie Bawalan were identified in this session.

meetings.title: Discussion with Djoey and Sue
meetings.summary: Jamie held a coaching check-in with Djoey (and Sue), reviewing Djoey's well-being (up to 7/10) and performance trajectory on the CDC case. Key positives noted: strong resilience, improved CTM presentation clarity, best qualitative data point to date from agent ethnography, and high coachability following last week's heavy 3-way feedback session. Areas to push in the final week include deepening agent interview synthesis into actionable pilot recommendations, sharpening CTM slides, and maintaining consistent (not spiked) improvement. Jamie committed to continuing detailed, week-by-week feedback and encouraged Djoey to hold future PLs to the same standard.

meetings.title: Media planning with Joran
meetings.summary: The meeting focused on finalizing the Iloilo smallholder rice farmer pitch deck and aligning on implementation details for the NAP proposal. Key decisions include structuring the pitch flow as Problem → Solution → Scaling Framework → Motivation → GEDSI → Delivery Plan, with the core message framing financial resilience through digital credit-linked production and guaranteed off-take. Capacity building lanes were mapped: EF/EFDD handles org strengthening and co-op formation, Land Bank covers financial literacy, and Mayani focuses on agronomic practices and tech adoption from Year 2 onwards. Land Bank is the primary credit partner with repayment tied to harvest proceeds mirroring the Tarlac model, and an MOU with RBC is needed to enable automatic deduction at point of sale; alternative financiers (RFC, ASA Philippines, ACC Foundation) were flagged if Land Bank is too slow. Open questions include confirming a pilot institutional off-taker in Iloilo (Raúl Báñez to be asked to identify one, e.g., a provincial hospital), securing an indicative floor price before the farm visit, and fleshing out the EFDD collaboration proposal to avoid duplication.

meetings.title: Bye-Bye Summit — AI transformation, Helix strategy, and case team demos
meetings.summary: The AP Energy PA is up 18% YTD, with Northeast Asia (Japan/Korea) growing 40–50%; the PA is targeting 20% full-year growth with an AI-transformation-heavy pipeline (Sembcorp, QGC, Korean value chain). Project Helix's knowledge layer aims to shift case knowledge capture from 10% to 80% via automated AI synthesis on case close, with Integrated Energy already in the prototype phase (100 cases ingested) and full energy practice onboarding expected in October. Two Helix tools are mature and available now: Size of the Prize (compresses trading diagnostics from weeks to hours, tested with ExxonMobil) and Networks AI (field force and capex optimization for utilities); teams should proactively reach out to leverage these in relevant client discussions. Three live demos showed practical AI use: an interactive semiconductor value chain HTML map built in a weekend via Claude prompting, an N8n newsletter digest workflow built in 30 minutes, and a Flask-based auto-refreshing resourcing dashboard linked to SharePoint Excel—all built without coding knowledge. Key open questions include how to scale Helix tool access autonomously to CCOs and case teams without bottlenecking on Vantage capacity, which is described as the current fix in progress.

meetings.title: AIP steering committee — governance updates, operating model, and capability building
meetings.summary: The AIP steering committee preparatory session covered three areas: STEERCO deck walkthrough, governance updates, and capability building session 1. On governance, Secretary Borja (CCC) confirmed willingness to co-chair the steering committee, elevating CCC to chair institution; DBM and DepDev were requested as additions to the STEERCO composition, and the TOR must be updated to reflect CCC's new role — DOF will conduct a bilateral with CCC early next week before recirculating the TOR to PBSP and PPP Center. The placeholder STEERCO date remains September 3rd, though TOR signing on that date is uncertain pending DOF and CCC guidance; Secretary Borja requested two pre-STEERCO briefing sessions (one with him, one with CCC technical team), likely DOF-CCC only. Jamie led the capability building session on origination and screening, covering the Philippines' key climate impact drivers, cost-of-inaction estimates (~$1.2–1.4T by 2030), and the protect/grow/participate private sector investment framework targeting a 3–6x BCR for agri-adaptation. Key open questions include: final STEERCO logistics lead (CCC vs. DOF), timeline for the CCC department circular formalizing AIP, and DOF's definitive position on its capacity/resourcing in the operating model.

meetings.title: Discussion with Alex

Key guidance included returning to pen-and-paper first, listing data inputs per sector against BSA/PCA, and developing proxies where data is unavailable (no such thing as an unsizable market). Jamie also reassured Alex that Max's evaluation is objective and continuous, covering the full staffing period — not a judgment on one or two days — and that Alex should openly show Max both Claude's and her own thinking rather than defaulting to Claude's output. Action needed: book December leaves immediately, and progress NAP market sizing with renewed ownership and rigor.

AI tooling (Claude) is gaining traction and the team is encouraged to explore further use cases including progress update agents and end-of-year boarding support.

meetings.title: Interview with Business Mirror
meetings.summary: Jamie gave a media interview to Andrea of Business Mirror on BCG Manila's 'Filipino Abroad' report, the 4th in the Filipino Dream series. Key talking points covered include the four OFW archetypes (family lifelines, long-haul guardians, anchored earners, self-builders), the complexity of the migration decision, and what would bring OFWs back (job confidence and safety-net infrastructure beyond salary). Jamie clarified the survey predates the Middle East conflict and that BCG does not forecast migration flows. No next report topic has been confirmed yet, though BCG Manila is open to a fifth installment or a cross-series trend review; this remains an open question for the team.

meetings.title: Investment strategies for regions
meetings.summary: The first AIP Steering Committee meeting presented progress on the Adaptation Investment Platform, covering two pilot projects in Iloilo (rice sector, ~8B pesos total investment over nine years) and Negros Occidental (sugarcane transition, ~90B over 12 years), with immediate funding targets of 1B and 1.2B respectively. Key governance decisions remain open: the committee must choose between anchoring the AIP under a Green Force instrument or a separate CCC instrument, with BCG/ECG to bring a recommendation to the senior committee. Secretariat funding (~400M) is still a critical gap, and ECG will shadow and hand over capacity over the next six to nine months while staffing is secured. Jamie's team is responsible for circulating the narrative write-up post-meeting, finalizing the project pipeline with assigned owners, and scheduling nine capability-building sessions including provincial site visits.

meetings.title: Debrief with James and Des from the SteerCo
meetings.summary: The NAP SteerCo meeting was deemed a strong success — all agencies aligned on the importance of the work, asked for more touchpoints, and PBSP's board chairman was briefed in real time. **Key immediate actions** center on a full working team debrief (Sept 10) covering the policy paper ownership, project co-lead assignments (PPP Center for Bukidnon and Isabela; PBSP pending Alvin dinner Sept 9), and named governance roles. A CCC bilateral (Sept 10, 11 AM) is needed to get Commissioner Herrera to designate focal points: Sandra for policy, Trina for finance/VAD, and a project lead. **Open questions** include whether PBSP can fund participation internally (to be resolved with Alvin), whether DOF's part-time person is confirmed as Jen, and which CCC teams to include in the working group. The SteerCo cadence shifts to bimonthly (Oct/Nov, Jan, Mar) with themed sessions and the site visit pushed to January/February to allow more capability building progress first.

meetings.title: CTM discussion
meetings.summary: The team reviewed the UK CTM report and found it strongly validates the AIP narrative, particularly on physical risk solutions; insurance was noted as too large-scale for current micro-level projects but a potential future platform-level entry point. A matching pathways framework (project archetypes → ecosystem mapping → matching logic → data-driven tool) was presented as the answer to James's sustainability question, with the framing to be forward-looking rather than retrospective. Dave raised the need for a formal sustainability embedding framework covering capacity building, budget, tools, and processes to proactively address recurring questions about AIP sustainability post-BCG. The biggest open risk is AIP institutionalization — agencies need legal documentation (e.g. a department order) to mandate participation and release budget, and CCC internal politics (climate finance team and Sec Borja's office not yet fully looped in) is a live threat; tomorrow's steering committee with Dave attending is critical to secure a verbal presidential mandate from Sec Borja. Jamie's hypothesis is that the hardest long-term challenge will be the matching piece itself — getting projects to secure the right financing, operators, and suppliers — which is harder than recruiting new projects and goes beyond the UK layer.

meetings.title: Discussion with Mitti labs
meetings.summary: Jamie met with Mitti Labs (Pelle, Yash, Bella) to align on piloting AWD carbon sequestration in Iloilo ahead of NEODIVE 9 hectarage limits, targeting 500 ha per irrigation system (up to 2,000–2,500 ha across 4 systems) with a longer-term goal of 25,000–30,000 ha. Key decisions include focusing the Monday September 7th Iloilo meeting with provincial agriculturist Jaron on AWD community benefits rather than documentation, with farmer carbon rights agreements handled progressively and directly between individual farmers and Mitti Labs. Open questions include whether Pelle can attend on Monday, whether Miami can provide meaningful Q4 ground presence given their non-rice focus, and how Peace and Equity Foundation can be integrated as a capacity-building partner. Jamie and team agreed the fastest scaling path — if Straw won't have full-time staff this year — is for Mitti Labs to fund Straw's dedicated resource, which Jamie will raise with Pelle.
